{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "---
name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build Docusaurus
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: docusaurus/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: docusaurus
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build website
        working-directory: docusaurus
        run: npm run build

      - name: Upload Build Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: docusaurus/build

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
    needs: build

    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write

    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5",
  "rationale": "The workflow already caches npm dependencies through setup-node's built-in `cache: npm`, so adding a separate dependency cache (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) is contraindicated because an equivalent cache already exists. The supported optimization that fits is P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: bound jobs with a custom timeout to reduce runaway consumption. Representative successful-duration history exists in ci_history (successful runs complete in roughly 1-2 minutes), so a 30-minute timeout provides ample operational headroom for valid builds including cold installs while bounding runaway jobs. The change preserves the intended build and deploy coverage, keeps all permissions and steps unchanged, and adds no secrets, privileged actions, publishing operations, or new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
